title: How Big Rapids Built a New K-5 Literacy Framework in One Day with Panorama Solara
summary: Discover how Big Rapids Public Schools transformed its K-5 literacy framework in just one day using Panorama Solara.
body_text: Serving 2,400 students in central Michigan, Big Rapids Public Schools has built a strong culture of collaboration around its multi-tiered system of supports (MTSS) . After using Panorama to support student interventions and data-driven decision-making, district leaders expanded their work with Solara , Panorama's AI platform. When Michigan's new literacy requirements prompted the district to redesign its elementary curriculum, Big Rapids Public Schools used Solara to build a new K-5 scope and sequence, streamline intervention planning, and give educators more time to focus on students. Challenges New state literacy laws required Big Rapids Public Schools to redesign its K-5 literacy scope and sequence and align instruction with evidence-based reading interventions before the start of the new school year. Educators were spending significant time creating curriculum resources, intervention materials, and planning documents from scratch, leaving less time to support students. Title teachers were responsible for creating Individual Reading Improvement Plans (IRIPs) for as many as 100 students in a single grade, requiring the district to temporarily reassign Title math teachers to help complete the workload before state deadlines. Solution Panorama Solara Results Big Rapids built a state-compliant K-5 literacy scope and sequence in a single day instead of spending the entire summer building it manually. The district created an IRIP tool that eliminated weeks of documentation work, allowing Title teachers to spend more time delivering interventions and supporting students. Teachers optimized time-consuming work with Solara, using it to create Lexile-adjusted text sets, generate standards-aligned science resources, and develop data-informed seating charts. By combining district curriculum, student data, and state guidelines in one platform, Big Rapids transformed Solara into a districtwide resource for curriculum development, intervention planning, and instructional decision-making. Challenges As Big Rapids strengthened its MTSS implementation, educators found themselves spending significant time creating and sourcing resources. Teachers managed curriculum documents, intervention materials, and planning tools across multiple buildings, often using their own spreadsheets or notes. "We were creating all of these things from scratch," said Elizabeth Robinson, MTSS Coordinator. "Most of our time was just spent creating something and not even using it yet, because it just took a long time to input data or create a structure." The challenge became even greater as Michigan's new literacy requirements prompted the district to reevaluate its elementary literacy curriculum. Big Rapids needed to identify instructional gaps, incorporate a new phonics curriculum, and redesign its K-5 scope and sequence—all before the new school year. At the same time, the district faced another significant challenge: creating Individual Reading Improvement Plans (IRIPs) for students requiring reading intervention. In some elementary grades, as many as 100 students qualified for IRIPs. The workload was so substantial that Big Rapids sometimes reassigned Title math teachers to help write reading plans in order to meet state deadlines. District leaders needed a faster way to organize curriculum, generate documentation, and personalize instruction without adding to teachers' workloads. Solution Big Rapids had already established Panorama as a key part of its MTSS framework, using the platform to identify students needing additional support and create consistent systems for intervention planning. When Panorama introduced Solara , district leaders saw an opportunity to build on that foundation by combining AI with the district's curriculum, resources, and student data. The district evaluated Solara through its MTSS decision-making process and involved educators across the district before moving forward. “We looked at Solara, and it was a winner,” Robinson said. “There was really no other option that could do the things that we needed it to do and still be linked to all of our student data." Big Rapids partnered with the Panorama team to create tools that integrated district curriculum and instructional resources. When the district adopted UFLI Foundations to strengthen foundational literacy instruction, Solara helped educators map the new materials alongside their existing curriculum, identify where new lessons were needed, and generate a complete K-5 scope and sequence aligned to district goals. District leaders appreciated that Solara was purpose-built for education. Unlike generic AI tools, Solara keeps educators focused on instructional work and student outcomes. “What I like about Solara is that it will say, ‘That's not an educational question. I can't answer that.’ It's an accountability measure. It allows us to keep using our critical thinking skills and be intentional with how much we're using AI ," Robinson said. Those guardrails gave educators confidence to expand Solara into new use cases, from differentiated instruction and intervention planning to science lessons and classroom organization. For Samantha Lipscomb, a high school science teacher, that meant using AI to handle the time-consuming groundwork while she remained responsible for instructional decisions. "I always joke and say that Solara is my clerical assistant," Lipscomb said. "It gives me that data right away, and then I can make my decisions from there." Results Built an elementary literacy framework in one day To meet Michigan's new literacy requirements, Big Rapids used Solara to build a complete K-5 scope and sequence and pacing guides before the start of the school year. “We were able to take the Public Act and plug it in [to Solara] to create resources that we know the state of Michigan would approve,” Robinson explained. “Then we could plug in the UFLI curriculum and have Solara fill in the holes to make us an entire curriculum for next year.” To prevent teachers from spending their summer rebuilding the curriculum, Robinson and MTSS Director Jaime Knape completed the work themselves in Solara in a single day. When asked how long the project would have taken without Solara, Robinson's answer was immediate: "The entire summer." Saved weeks of work creating IRIPs Using Solara, Big Rapids transformed one of its most time-intensive literacy workflows. Big Rapids developed an IRIP tool that generates draft reading plans using student assessment data, allowing educators to review and refine plans rather than writing each one from scratch. The process now saves Title teachers weeks of work during one of the busiest times of the school year. Instead of racing to complete paperwork before parent conferences, Title teachers can now focus on providing interventions and supporting students. Expanded Solara into everyday teaching Once educators saw what Solara could do, they began applying it to challenges across the district. Lipscomb uses Solara to streamline lesson planning while keeping her own expertise at the center. For one earth science unit, she input notes from her textbook and information from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to generate standards-aligned text sets tailored to her students’ Lexile levels. "It's been really helpful because finding good texts that then can be adjusted based on Lexile level is invaluable," Lipscomb said. “What I really like about Solara is that I can attach a class and say, 'How can I address this particular text with this group of students based on NWEA MAP scores?'” Lipscomb has also used Solara to generate unit-by-unit laboratory activities that fit within a 60-minute class period, helping her incorporate more hands-on learning while staying aligned to her curriculum. At the start of the school year, she even used attendance, behavior, and academic data already in Solara to create classroom seating charts tailored to her students' needs. "The first time I did it, I did not have to change the seating chart for weeks," Lipscomb said. "It was a total lifesaver." What began as a solution for one literacy initiative has become part of how Big Rapids approaches problem-solving across the district. "We have thrown absolutely everything at it," Robinson said. " Now if we have an idea, we wonder how Solara can make this easier for us."

title: SCCAI Score for Ulcerative Colitis: What the Questions Mean
summary: Understand every SCCAI component and what the symptom score cannot prove.
body_text: The Simple Clinical Colitis Activity Index, or SCCAI, summarizes the daily symptom burden of ulcerative colitis. It asks about daytime and nighttime bowel movements, urgency, blood, general well-being, and specified symptoms outside the bowel. It does not include a colonoscopy, CRP, ESR, CBC, albumin, or fecal calprotectin. A low SCCAI can therefore indicate limited symptoms without proving that the colon is healed, while a higher score can be influenced by problems other than active UC ( IBD activity-index review ). What the six SCCAI areas mean Daytime stool frequency and nighttime stool frequency are scored separately. That distinction captures a burden missed by tools that ask only for a daily total. Urgency is graded from none through immediate need or incontinence. Rectal bleeding is graded by frequency and amount. General well-being records the person’s overall sense of health. The final area adds points for selected extraintestinal features , such as joint, eye, or skin manifestations. Because wording and response options matter, use the actual questionnaire rather than reconstructing it from memory. Record whether a night stool woke you from sleep, whether blood was streaked, obvious, or passed without stool, and whether urgency caused leakage. Infection, bowel preparation, laxatives, menstrual symptoms, pelvic-floor dysfunction, and other conditions can affect answers. Common research interpretation treats scores of 2 or less as remission, with increasing ranges used for mild, moderate, and severe activity. However, cutoffs vary across validation studies and uses. A change over time on the same version is often more informative than applying an isolated internet label. SCCAI versus Mayo and UC PRO-2 SCCAI contains more symptom detail than UC PRO-2. UC PRO-2 focuses on stool frequency and rectal bleeding, while SCCAI also captures nighttime stools, urgency, general well-being, and extraintestinal manifestations. Partial Mayo uses stool frequency, rectal bleeding, and a physician global assessment. The scales are not interchangeable even when they move in the same direction ( PRO-2 and mucosal-healing study ; Mayo-score comparison ). SCCAI is noninvasive and convenient for repeat measurement. Its deliberate lack of endoscopy also limits what “remission” means. Endoscopic activity is scored separately with MES or UCEIS , and biopsy activity with a histology index such as Nancy or Robarts ( endoscopic activity review ). Why labs remain separate Fecal calprotectin and CRP provide objective inflammatory context but do not alter SCCAI points. AGA guidance recommends combining symptoms with biomarkers during UC monitoring, including when symptoms and inflammation may disagree ( AGA UC biomarker guidance ). STRIDE-II similarly treats symptom response, biomarker change, and healing as distinct targets ( STRIDE-II ). Keep the six component answers, date, medication changes, and unusual circumstances beside the total. Add calprotectin, CRP, CBC, albumin, endoscopy, and biopsy results from the same period. Contact your care team promptly for rapidly increasing bowel frequency, substantial bleeding, fever, severe pain or swelling, fainting, or dehydration. SCCAI makes the patient experience visible and repeatable. It becomes safer and more clinically useful when it is read as a symptom score, not a substitute for inflammatory testing. Questions that make the number more useful Before comparing this result with an older one, confirm that both records used the same named instrument, version, scoring range, and assessment window. Ask whether the total represents the worst segment, a sum across segments, an average, or a single day. If a clinician or study used a modified version, record exactly what was removed or added. Also check whether treatment, bowel preparation, infection, missed diary entries, or incomplete examination affected the inputs. A small apparent change may reflect measurement conditions rather than a meaningful change in disease. At a visit, useful questions include: What domain does this score measure? Which component drove the result? What would count as response or remission in this setting? Does the number need confirmation with blood work, stool testing, endoscopy, biopsy, or imaging? Is the goal to follow symptoms, current inflammation, structural damage, treatment response, or quality of life? Asking these questions turns an unfamiliar total into a specific clinical conversation. For personal tracking, avoid combining unlike scores on one graph. Keep each instrument in its own series and place objective tests on parallel timelines. Save the source report because the component details may matter later. Note both the sample or procedure date and the date you received the result. Trends are easiest to interpret when the method and timing stay consistent. If the number conflicts with how you feel or with another test, bring the disagreement to your care team instead of choosing the result that seems most reassuring. Discordance is often the reason to look more closely. This article is for educational purposes and is not medical advice. It is researched against current AGA clinical guidelines and peer-reviewed sources. Always discuss treatment decisions with your care team. title: America’s Sound, Heard Around the World
summary: Spotify is proud to be a home for American culture. As the nation marks its 250th anniversary, we wanted to take a look at how American artists, creators, and authors shape listening at home and around the world. America leads the charts, at home and abroad On any given day, people across 184 markets open...
body_text: Spotify is proud to be a home for American culture. As the nation marks its 250th anniversary, we wanted to take a look at how American artists, creators, and authors shape listening at home and around the world. America leads the charts, at home and abroad On any given day, people across 184 markets open Spotify and reach for something made in America. From songwriters outside Nashville to podcasters recording across the Rocky Mountains, from audiobook authors in New England to hip-hop producers in Atlanta, American artists, creators, and authors power what the world listens to. Americans love listening to American music, and the numbers are striking: 69% of all streams in the country go to American artists, and American music makes up 70% of the Spotify Top 50 chart in the U.S. in 2025. Listeners in the South and Midwest stream the most music made in America: In just the past week, Mississippi topped the list, followed by West Virginia, South Dakota, Alabama, and Louisiana. The artists driving those numbers capture the breadth of the American sound: Taylor Swift tops the charts both domestically and globally, while Bad Bunny , Morgan Wallen , Kendrick Lamar , and Post Malone are among the top most-streamed American artists in the U.S. Notably, Morgan Wallen has an exceptionally strong home-market audience, with 74% of his streams coming from U.S. listeners, which is the highest share among American artists. The story doesn’t stop at the border. The United States is the world’s top exporter of music, and Spotify, which drives more music industry revenue than any other company, is what takes it everywhere. Beyond Taylor Swift, Bad Bunny, Ariana Grande , Billie Eilish , and Eminem are among the most-streamed American artists of all time globally. In the past year alone, people outside the U.S. streamed songs featuring at least one American artist 776 billion times. Pop, hip-hop, rock, indie, and country are the American genres most streamed domestically. Internationally, pop, hip-hop, rock, dance, and indie lead, and over the last five years, streams of American country music have grown more than 94% outside the U.S. Every Independence Day, Americans cue up more than 650,000 Fourth of July playlists celebrating cookouts, block parties, road trips, and fireworks. Top searched tracks during the holiday include Bruce Springsteen ‘s “ Born in the U.S.A. ,” Lee Greenwood ‘s “ God Bless The U.S.A. ,” Katy Perry ‘s “ Firework ,” John Mellencamp ‘s “ R.O.C.K. In The U.S.A. ,” and Ray Charles ‘ “ America the Beautiful ,” representing a playlist that spans decades but pulses with the same spirit. American voices in every format The reach of American creators on Spotify extends well beyond music. U.S.-created podcasts have been streamed in more than 180 countries so far in 2026, with The Joe Rogan Experience , The Mel Robbins Podcast , This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von , Huberman Lab , and Call Her Daddy leading Spotify’s global charts. The U.S. is Spotify’s number one podcast market in the world. Many Americans feature on our global list of the top audiobooks of all time, with American author Sarah J. Maas being the most listened-to author of all time on Spotify. Works by American authors Freida McFadden ( The Housemaid ), Rebecca Yarros ( Fourth Wing ), Jennette McCurdy ( I’m Glad My Mom Died ), and James Clear ( Atomic Habits ) all feature on the global all-time list. Investing in the people behind the culture Celebrating American culture means investing in the people who create it. Spotify paid music rightsholders more than $11 billion in 2025, which is more in a single year than any company has ever paid. Much of that has flowed to American rightsholders: Royalties generated by U.S. artists from Spotify alone have more than doubled since 2019, with nearly half coming from listeners outside the U.S. Spotify is proud to help export American music and culture around the world. Beyond the dollars, Spotify invests in the infrastructure that American artists and creators need for sustainable careers. Spotify for Artists gives musicians access to listener data and global promotional tools. Human editorial teams and programs like EQUAL and Fresh Finds have helped surface and invest in emerging American talent. Features like Reserved help real fans get real tickets to their favorite artists’ live shows in the U.S., while SongDNA lets listeners explore the writers, producers, and collaborators behind any song. Across the country, Spotify has doubled down our investment in podcast creators. Earlier this year, Spotify opened Sycamore Studios In Los Angeles , a podcast production hub where guests like Snoop Dogg and author Andy Weir have recorded, alongside dozens of local creators. Spotify’s audiobook investment has made books more accessible globally while unlocking new revenue for authors and publishers, driving up to 30% annual growth in the U.S. and paying out hundreds of millions of dollars to authors and publishers annually. As AI reshapes the creative landscape, Spotify supports unlocking new ways for artists to create and for listeners to discover, while aggressively protecting against the misuse of generative AI. New initiatives like Artist Profile Protection , Verified by Spotify, and AI Credits , combined with our industry-leading policies , altogether strengthen protections for American artists, podcasters, and authors, and increase transparency for fans. A stage the size of the world From the blues to hip-hop, from the gramophone to podcasts, American culture never stops evolving, and Spotify has been proud to be the place where that evolution lives, streams, and spreads. On America’s 250th birthday, we celebrate every songwriter who poured their heart out onto a page, every artist who ever played a small stage hoping someone would listen, every podcaster who hits record with a story to tell, and every author whose words find a reader halfway across the world. Spotify exists to give all of them, regardless of label, budget, or background, a stage the size of the world. Happy Fourth of July, and here’s to the next 250 years of American sound!

title: Direct Sourcing + EOR: Why They're Better Together
summary: Direct sourcing finds your contract talent; an EOR employs it compliantly. Here's why running them together cuts cost and risk — and how HireArt does it.
body_text: Direct sourcing and employer of record (EOR) employment are two of the highest-leverage moves in contingent workforce management — and they make a beautiful couple. Direct sourcing describes how a company fills contract roles from its own talent pool instead of paying a staffing agency's markup. An EOR is the entity that legally employs those workers and absorbs the compliance, payroll, and benefits burden that comes with them. One answers where the talent comes from. The other answers who employs it and carries the risk. Most companies treat these as separate projects, run on separate systems, owned by separate teams. That separation is exactly where the value springs a leak. Sourcing a great contractor directly does nothing for you if employing them is still slow, risky, and expensive. Even the most efficient EOR in the world can't help you if you're still routing every requisition through agencies at full markup. Put together, direct sourcing and EOR don't just add up — they compound. What is Direct Sourcing? Direct sourcing is the practice of filling contingent roles from a company's own private talent pool rather than routing every hire through a staffing agency. Staffing Industry Analysts defines it as leveraging your own brand and private candidate pool to place talent into the organization as temporary workers. These pools are private and not available to the open labor market. The economics are the headline. Traditional staffing markups on temporary and contract roles commonly run 25–50% or higher on the bill rate, and each requisition starts from scratch. Direct sourcing collapses that. According to AMS, a talent solutions firm, enterprises with mature direct sourcing programs typically cut contingent labor costs 15–40% versus traditional agency models, fill 20–40% of repeat roles from pre-vetted candidates within the first year, and reduce time-to-hire by up to 60%. The quality case is just as strong. A direct talent pool is made of people you've already vetted. This could include former contractors who performed, candidates who narrowly missed a full-time offer, referrals who already understand your business. They ramp faster and stay longer than cold agency placements because the relationship isn't starting at zero. What is an Employer of Record (EOR)? An employer of record is a third party that becomes the legal employer of a company's contract workers . The EOR handles payroll, taxes, benefits, onboarding, offboarding, and HR compliance, while the client directs the day-to-day work. A modern EOR also indemnifies the client against HR compliance risk, meaning misclassification exposure, wage-and-hour liability, and regulatory complexity shift off the client's balance sheet. This is the half of the equation companies tend to underestimate. There's a persistent tendency to conflate EOR with "payroll," but compliant, hourly, multi-state employment is genuinely complex. An EOR lets a company scale its contract workforce up or down with project demand, expand into new states without standing up legal entities, and offer competitive benefits without rewriting its own policies. The administrative weight of onboarding, compliance, time-and-attendance, and offboarding moves to a partner built to carry it. Why Direct Sourcing and EOR Usually Live in Separate Systems In most programs, direct sourcing and EOR are bolted together rather than built together. A company buys a direct sourcing tool or stands up a talent community on one platform, then hands selected candidates off to a separate EOR vendor to actually employ them. The two systems don't share a data model, a worker record, or a workflow. That handoff is where things break. The candidate experience fractures between "you've been selected" and "you're now employed." Hiring managers lose visibility the moment a worker crosses from sourcing into employment. The compliance check happens in one place and the offer in another, so classification decisions get disconnected from the people making the hire. Every gap between systems is an opportunity for delay, error, and a worse worker experience to creep in. That worker experience reputation is what determines whether that person ever comes back into your pool. Why They're Better Together When direct sourcing and EOR run on a single platform, the handoff disappears. In this new partnership, sourcing a worker and compliantly employing them become one continuous workflow. The classification assessment, the offer, onboarding, and benefits enrollment all happen against the same worker record, in the same system. There's no vendor-to-vendor black box in the middle. That integration produces three immediate wins: Speed. There's no re-keying of data or waiting on a separate EOR to spin up an engagement. A directly sourced candidate can move from selected to employed in one flow. One client cut average onboarding time by more than eight business days simply by consolidating sourcing and employment with automated background checks in a single platform. Compliance by default. When employment is built into the same workflow as sourcing, classification and indemnification aren't an afterthought handled by a different vendor . They're part of the act of hiring. The risk is absorbed from the beginning, instead of being patched in later or "when needed." A continuous worker experience. The contractor deals with one system and one support team from first contact through final paycheck. That continuity is what makes them willing to come back. This is the entire engine behind a self-renewing talent pool! The Compounding Effect of Direct Sourcing + EOR The real reason direct sourcing and EOR belong together is the same reason that power couples thrive. Over time, each one makes the other better. This is a flywheel that a fragmented setup could never spin. Good EOR employment produces a good contractor experience. A good experience causes contractors to return for future engagements, which grows your direct talent pool. A larger, higher-quality pool means you can fill a larger share of roles directly, cutting agency markup. Finally, the more roles you fill from people you already know perform, the less ramp time and fewer performance problems you absorb. See why we're calling this partnership beautiful? Direct sourcing lowers cost. EOR lowers risk and raises retention. Together, the savings and the talent quality feed each other every cycle. Why Adoption Has Lagged — How to Close the Gap Direct sourcing is widely recognized as a top contingent workforce trend, yet end-to-end adoption remains low. What gives? The missing piece is usually the employment layer. Ardent Partners and the Future of Work Exchange found that only 11% of enterprises have a fully implemented, end-to-end direct sourcing program, while another 23% have some elements in place. At the same time, Staffing Industry Analysts reports that a majority of contingent leaders plan to invest in direct sourcing within two years. The intent is there. TYhe operational follow-through is not. The reason for the gap is rarely sourcing technology itself. It's that companies build a way to find talent without an integrated way to employ it compliantly — so the program stalls at pilot scale. Let Direct Sourcing and Staffing Partners Complement One Another Closing the gap doesn't require ripping out your agencies. Direct sourcing is a complement to staffing partners, not a wholesale replacement. Direct sourcing is strongest for repeatable, higher-volume, and niche-skill roles where a curated pool compounds in value. Meanwhile, trusted agencies still matter for one-off and urgent placements. Your "winners" are pairing a direct sourcing engine with embedded employment infrastructure while keeping a managed supplier network alongside it. How HireArt Combines Direct Sourcing and EOR HireArt was built around exactly this integration: sourcing and EOR employment live in one platform, not two. The HireArt platform combines the capabilities of an ATS with those of an HRIS, designed solely for managing contract workforces. This winning combination allows a company to run sourcing, employment, compliance, and worker support from a single source of truth. The HireArt Blended Solution On the sourcing side, HireArt blends three channels in one interface: an experienced in-house recruiting team, a curated network of 100+ vetted staffing partners, and the option to fold in a client's own preferred suppliers. On the employment side, HireArt acts as a modern EOR — managing the full lifecycle of payroll, taxes, benefits, and HR support, with full indemnification for HR compliance risk. Because both halves share one worker record, a candidate moves from sourced to employed in a single workflow, and the contractor stays in the same system from onboarding through offboarding. The pricing reflects the same logic. HireArt uses transparent, cost-plus pricing, and the sourcing fee applies only to a HireArt-sourced worker's first 2,080 hours logged or 52 weeks worked — after which you keep the worker with no ongoing sourcing markup. The platform itself is free when combined with EOR, AOR, or freelancer payments, so the technology layer isn't a separate line item. The Numbers Don't Lie The results show up in the numbers. A leading robotics company centralized its contractors on HireArt and reached a 94% retention rate, 35% year-over-year savings, an 88.9 contractor NPS, and 17 additional months of average contract length. A leading AI company that had struggled with a large global staffing firm moved to HireArt and saw $900,000 in annual savings across 2,650 contractors. Another infrastructure-technology company used HireArt to expand into 85 cities while lifting retention to 91%. Across its client base, HireArt customers save an average of 16.6% on contingent workforce costs, with much of that coming from eliminating agency markup on directly sourced roles. That's the case for togetherness in practice: direct sourcing brings the cost and quality advantage, EOR brings the compliance and experience advantage, and a single platform turns the two into a compounding system rather than two disconnected tools. Bada-bing. Ready to run direct sourcing and EOR employment in one workflow instead of two? See how HireArt makes it work.

title: What Does UGC Creator Mean? A Complete Guide for 2026
summary: Learn what a UGC creator does, which skills matter, and how brands use tools like Reacher to manage UGC campaigns.
body_text: Finding UGC Jobs and Sharing Performance Data Top Platforms and Marketplaces for UGC Creators For creators ready to monetize their skills, identifying reliable platforms is essential. Marketplaces like TikTok Creator Marketplace, Instagram’s branded content tools, and specialized platforms focused on UGC offer structured access to brands seeking authentic content. These platforms connect creators with campaigns that fit their niche and style, simplifying the process of finding paid UGC jobs. But, not all platforms operate equally. TikTok Creator Marketplace excels in matching creators with brand campaigns using performance signals and audience alignment, while Instagram’s branded content tools provide direct collaboration options but often favor creators with established followings. Niche platforms dedicated solely to UGC creators emphasize authentic content production without requiring influencer-level audience size. Beyond these, freelance marketplaces like Upwork or Fiverr sometimes list UGC creation projects, but they lack built-in performance tracking and brand integration features. For creators serious about long-term growth and strategic positioning, aligning with platforms that emphasize data-driven creator-brand matches is critical. Why Sharing Performance Data Gives You a Competitive Edge In a crowded creator market, transparency is a differentiator. Providing brands with detailed performance data. Such as engagement rates, click-throughs, and conversion metrics. From previous campaigns demonstrates professionalism and builds trust. This data acts as social proof of your content’s effectiveness, moving negotiations beyond subjective opinions to objective results. Brands increasingly demand measurable ROI from UGC partnerships. Creators who proactively share performance analytics position themselves as partners invested in brand success rather than just content producers. This strategy can justify higher rates and foster repeat collaborations. It also helps brands optimize campaigns by identifying which creator content drives the most impact, a important insight for scaling UGC programs efficiently. Tools like Reacher’s AI Creator Search enable brands to evaluate creators based on precise performance metrics. Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), engagement, and posting frequency. Making transparent data sharing a natural fit for creators aiming to stand out. Aligning your workflow with brands that use such advanced vetting technology ensures your content is valued and your partnerships are strategic. Pros and Cons of Popular UGC Platforms Pros Direct access to brand campaigns tailored to creator niches Built-in tools for campaign management and payment processing Performance tracking improves credibility and negotiation power Some platforms support creators without large followings Competition is high; standing out requires strategy and data sharing Some marketplaces favor creators with existing audiences Freelance platforms lack integrated performance analytics Manual outreach may still be necessary for niche or emerging brands

title: Fozzy Group повышает производительность складов на 20 % с помощью Zebra Technologies
summary: Комплекс решений для мобильной работы на базе Android™ обеспечивает максимальную окупаемость инвестиций и качество обслуживания клиентов.
body_text: Комплекс решений для мобильной работы на базе Android™ обеспечивает максимальную окупаемость инвестиций и качество обслуживания клиентов БОРН ЭНД, Великобритания – 17 Июнь 2020 – Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA), инновационная компания, чьи решения и партнеры позволяют коммерческим предприятиям добиваться максимальных результатов в своей работе, объявила, что одна из крупнейших розничных компаний Украины Fozzy Group воспользовалась решениями Zebra для мобильной работы. В число этих решений вошли мобильные компьютеры на базе Android, ручные сканеры, защитное ПО, услуги поддержки и настраиваемое ПО для голосового управления. Они были призваны повысить эффективность рабочих процессов в рамках стратегии модернизации склада. Около 1000 сотрудников Fozzy Group перешли на эти решения, и производительность труда выросла на 20 %. «Сейчас Fozzy Group использует передовое мобильное решение Zebra на базе Android и решение для голосового управления. Их развернула компания U & SLUNO sa.s., участник программы PartnerConnect, на платформе независимого поставщика ПО Symphony RetailAI. Эти решения позволяют модернизировать склады и сохранять лидирующие позиции на розничном рынке, — говорит Мачей Гавронски (Maciej Gawronski), управляющий цепочками поставок в Fozzy Group. — Решение увеличило производительность труда на 20 %, а благодаря защитному ПО и услугам поддержки общая выгода от приобретения стала еще выше». Из-за использования мобильных компьютеров разных марок эта компания, которая владеет 700 розничными магазинами, столкнулась с трудностями голосового управления и нуждалась в решении для оптимизации работы складов и магазинов. С этой целью Fozzy Group развернула компьютеры TC52 с сенсорным экраном и мобильные компьютеры MC3300 от Zebra. Решение также включает приложение LifeGuard для установки обновлений безопасности Android по воздуху, ПО Mobility DNA для оптимизации корпоративных приложений и рабочих процессов, а также услуги расширенной технической поддержки Zebra OneCare . Эти уникальные приложения и услуги помогают Fozzy Group добиться максимальной окупаемости инвестиций благодаря оптимизации работы ИТ-специалистов и сотрудников. «Инвестировав в эти решения, Fozzy Group сделала операции более эффективными, а заодно повысила качество обслуживания и уровень удовлетворенности клиентов, — говорит Фред Бисмут (Fred Bismuth), вице-президент и директор по продажам, Zebra Technologies в восточном регионе — Переход на устройства Zebra на базе Android и настраиваемое ПО для голосового управления помогают оптимизировать работу, а средства защиты LifeGuard и услуги поддержки OneCare обеспечивают непрерывную работу бизнеса». ОСНОВНЫЕ ВЫВОДЫ Fozzy Group развернула решения Zebra для мобильной работы в рамках стратегии модернизации склада и добилась роста производительности на 20 %. ПО LifeGuard для обеспечения безопасности и услуги Zebra OneCare помогают сократить совокупную стоимость владения и повысить общую выгоду от вложений. Предоставляя сотрудникам складов новые возможности, Fozzy Group стремится повысить качество обслуживания клиентов в нескольких каналах и точках взаимодействия. ### О КОМПАНИИ ZEBRA Zebra (NASDAQ: ZBRA) повышает качество работы с клиентами в рознице, онлайн-коммерции, производстве, транспортировке и логистике, здравоохранении и иных отраслях промышленности и вдохновляет на достижение максимальной эффективности. Имея более десяти тысяч партнеров в 100 странах, мы поставляем адаптированные под различные отрасли промышленности комплексные решения, которые обеспечивают взаимосвязь между людьми, активами и данными, помогая нашим клиентам принимать особо важные для бесперебойной деятельности решения. Наши лидирующие на рынке решения поднимают качество обслуживания клиентов на новый уровень, помогают отслеживать и управлять запасами, повышают эффективность цепочек поставки и качество медицинского обслуживание пациентов.
